`cost_per_1m_txn_usd` extrapolates the measured per-call cost to one million transactions; classic GBM has no API cost (local compute only). `cost_per_caught_fraud_usd` = API spend / true positives on the eval sets.

### Which model is best?

- **Best accuracy (F1):** `classic_gbm` with mean F1 0.941 (range 0.909 to 0.991), precision 0.891, recall 1.000.
- **Fastest per transaction:** `classic_gbm` at 0.1 ms median.
- **Cheapest API option:** `jev` at $0.0219 per 1,000 transactions (about $22 per million).
- **Most accurate API option:** `gpt-6-luna` (F1 0.830, $0.1032 per 1,000).
- **Best F1 per dollar among API options:** `jev` (31.2 F1 points per $ per 1k transactions).

Head-to-head among API systems (ratios are first / second):

- `gpt-6-luna` vs `jev`: 4.7x cost, 16.4x latency, F1 0.830 vs 0.685
- `claude-sonnet-5-5` vs `gpt-6-luna`: 21.1x cost, 0.6x latency, F1 0.820 vs 0.830
- `claude-sonnet-5-5` vs `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`: 10.5x cost, 1.6x latency, F1 0.820 vs 0.775
- `claude-sonnet-5-5` vs `jev`: 99.4x cost, 10.3x latency, F1 0.820 vs 0.685
- `claude-haiku-5-5` vs `gpt-6-luna`: 1.1x cost, 0.5x latency, F1 0.796 vs 0.830
- `claude-haiku-5-5` vs `claude-sonnet-5-5`: 0.1x cost, 0.8x latency, F1 0.796 vs 0.820
- `claude-haiku-5-5` vs `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`: 0.5x cost, 1.2x latency, F1 0.796 vs 0.775
- `claude-haiku-5-5` vs `jev`: 5.1x cost, 7.8x latency, F1 0.796 vs 0.685
- `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` vs `gpt-6-luna`: 2.0x cost, 0.4x latency, F1 0.775 vs 0.830
- `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` vs `jev`: 9.5x cost, 6.6x latency, F1 0.775 vs 0.685

**Overall:** `classic_gbm` gives the best accuracy on this data, and is also the fastest, with no per-call API spend.

Among API-based systems the F1 leader is `gpt-6-luna`, behind `classic_gbm` by 0.111 F1.

**How to read this fairly**

- The classic GBM is trained on labelled history; JEV and Claude run with no training data (zero-shot, prompt only). If you have no labels yet, the zero-shot systems are the only option.
- Eval sets are fraud-enriched, so precision here is higher than it would be at the real 0.5 to 3% fraud rate. Compare systems with each other, not with production precision.
- Differences of a few F1 points on a few hundred rows are within noise; the F1 range column shows the iteration-to-iteration spread.
- JEV cost uses the vendor list price of $0.042/MTok input and free output; Claude cost uses measured `usage` tokens at list prices with cache read/write adjustments.
